warningMessage: Salt inclusion exceeding 0.5% causes electrolyte imbalance, severe wet droppings, and potential sodium toxicity.
Cottonseed meal contains free gossypol which suppresses egg yolk quality and induces liver/heart toxicity at high levels.
Fish meal above 5% risks causing off-flavors ('fishy taint') in eggs and poultry meat, and potential gizzerosine toxicity.
High barley levels contain beta-glucans which increase gut viscosity; requires enzyme supplementation if exceeded.
Blood meal above 3% reduces feed palatability and can cause severe amino acid unbalance.
Meat and bone meal capped at 5% to prevent severe ash spikes and uncontrolled calcium/phosphorus distortion.
Grower/Starter Ca:AvailP ratio must stay between 1.5:1 and 2.2:1 for optimal bone mineralization without tying up phosphorus.
Active Layer Ca:AvailP ratio must stay between 7:1 and 11:1 to sustain shell quality without causing kidney failure.

This ration includes a cattle-formulated feed. Cattle mineral mixes carry far more copper than sheep can tolerate and are a common cause of fatal copper toxicity in sheep - do not share cattle feed with sheep.

This ration includes a goat-formulated feed. Goats tolerate more copper than sheep do, so goat mineral mixes can still be too high in copper for sheep - check the label before sharing feed between the two.

This ration includes a general trace mineral premix. Confirm it is labeled copper-free/sheep-safe before using it - most all-species and cattle/goat trace mineral packs carry more copper than sheep can safely handle.
Canola meal contains glucosinolates, which can suppress thyroid function and growth at high inclusion - keep it under roughly 10% of the ration, especially for poultry and swine.

Raw/untoasted soybeans contain trypsin inhibitors that block protein digestion and stunt growth, especially in young monogastrics. Use toasted soybean meal instead unless this batch has been heat-processed.

This ration's Copper:Molybdenum ratio is outside the safe range for sheep (roughly 3:1 to 10:1). Below 3:1 risks copper deficiency (swayback, poor wool); above 10:1 - especially with total dietary copper over 10-15 ppm DM - risks fatal copper toxicity, since molybdenum is what keeps copper from accumulating in the liver.

This ration's Calcium:Oxalate ratio is below the safe minimum (0.5:1) - oxalates in the forage are binding dietary calcium faster than it's being supplied. In horses this causes 'Big Head' disease (nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism); in ruminants it can cause hypocalcemia. Aim for a ratio above 1:1 by adding a calcium source or cutting back on high-oxalate grasses (Setaria, Buffel, Kikuyu, Pangola).

Sorghum-sudangrass is a nitrate accumulator - risk spikes after drought, frost, heavy nitrogen fertilization, or on lush new regrowth (conditions this app has no way to check). If any of those apply, get it lab-tested for nitrate-N before feeding: under ~700 ppm is generally safe, over ~2,500 ppm is acute-toxicity danger. Don't feed untested to pregnant ruminants.
